notes.summary: Exact-source audit: over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, BJ already constructs genuine finite-energy MA on singular integral projective varieties; existence is equivalent to the envelope property, conjectured for unibranch varieties in the saved v4. BFJ saved v1 retains smoothness, algebraizability and SNC-support hypotheses.
notes.detailedSummary: Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4 gives energy, finite-energy MA, locality, comparison and downward energy differentiation without smoothness, but general surjectivity requires the envelope property (Theorem 12.8), which also implies unibranchness (Theorem 5.12). Lemma 5.13 assumes envelopes on the target and cannot supply them by circular normalization descent. The supplied 1201.0188 is v1, whose equation theorem is smooth, discretely valued, residue-characteristic-zero, function-field algebraizable and SNC-dual-complex-supported. Boucksom–Eriksson 1805.01016v3 treats continuous metrics and norms; the synthetic 2307.01697v1 completes measures rather than proving actual-potential surjectivity. These source facts delimit, but do not solve, the original atom.
notes.text:
The exact saved source Boucksom–Jonsson, Global pluripotential theory over a trivially valued field, arXiv:1801.08229v4 (watermark 22 March 2022), works over an algebraically closed trivially valued field. For an integral projective X and ample L, let V=(L^n). Its normalized energy satisfies E(0)=0 and E(φ+c)=E(φ)+c. Its operator is probability-normalized; the genuine raw operator is V MA. The raw measure condition is μ(X^an)=V and sup_{φ∈E¹}[E(φ)−V⁻¹∫φ dμ]<∞. Theorem 7.18 and Proposition 7.19 construct the finite-energy operator and its decreasing continuity, raw mass and normalization pushforward on possibly singular X. Theorems 7.40/7.44 give locality/comparison. Theorem 8.5 and Corollary 8.6 differentiate downward energy, with envelope identification requiring envelope regularity.

Theorem A states an embedding with dense image and says it is onto “if X is smooth, and either char k = 0 or dim X ≤ 2.” Theorem 12.8 proves that surjectivity is equivalent to the envelope property; Theorem 5.11 equates that property with weak compactness. Theorem 5.12 makes unibranchness necessary, and Conjecture 5.14 reads “If X is unibranch, then the envelope property holds for all θ ∈ N¹(X).” Lemma 5.13 assumes envelope properties on classes approaching the target class. Using that lemma to establish envelopes on the same target by normalization would be circular.

For the curve argument below the exact published inputs are Example 2.5 (flag-ideal PL functions on singular X), Example 2.6 (ray generators on smooth curves), Proposition 3.6(vi) (nef reflection for an already descended target PL function), Proposition 3.10 (uniform approximation by ample model functions in a fixed ample class), Theorem 4.15(iii) and decreasing closure (regularization), Example 4.13 (smooth-curve slope criterion), Theorem 5.20 and Lemma 5.17 (smooth envelopes and continuity), Proposition 7.2, equation (7.5) (energy projection), Proposition 7.19, equation (7.18) (genuine MA projection), and Proposition 12.7 (strong continuity). The new note proves all normalization applications rather than assuming arbitrary upstairs potentials descend.

The supplied 1201.0188 PDF is actual v1: its watermark is 30 December 2011 although its internal date is 29 October 2018. Its Theorem A assumes complete discrete valuation, residue characteristic zero, smooth projective X admitting descent to a one-variable function field completed by K, ample L, raw mass deg_L X, and support on the dual complex of an SNC model. L need not descend. This v1 is not an arbitrary-support finite-energy existence theorem. The supplied 1201.0187v2 similarly retains smooth projective, discretely valued, residue-characteristic-zero hypotheses for compactness/regularization.

1805.01016v3 is Boucksom–Eriksson, Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry. Its Theorem A concerns continuous psh metrics on geometrically reduced projective schemes; Corollary B retains continuity of envelopes. Its continuous energy projection formula is not a finite-energy singular equation theorem. Synthetic 2307.01697v1, Theorem A, establishes density and completeness on the measure side, not surjectivity from actual singular-space potentials. Pille–Schneider 2209.04879v2, Remark 4.4, distinguishes arbitrary-field finite-energy spaces from the unknown general extended operator. Gubler–Rabinoff 2506.13548v2 (17 September 2025) explicitly excludes constructing MA from that paper's singular-curve subharmonic results.

All ten authorized source-cache hashes match the supplied hashes. Twenty-one literal selected extracts, their line/character/PDF-page locators, published proofs, precise application checks and five fresh PDF-page extractions are in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. The saved PDF page 35 was visually checked for Proposition 3.6(vi) and its proof. Run python3 init_workspace.py and python3 provenance.py to reproduce the inventory and extracts. Source matches and execution do not verify the mathematics. No assertion is made about every later source outside the authorized caches.

notes.summary: Proved partial sector: actual integral projective unibranch curves over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, with ample L. Genuine raw MA is bijective modulo constants onto mass V=deg L measures with finite dual energy; E*(μ/V)=Σ∫μ_q((t,∞])²dt/(2V). All curve normalization and analytic-input descents are proved; higher-dimensional/discretely-valued P16.1 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Point ideals on singular X isolate the normalization rays after division by their positive integer orders. This proves PL descent, then model-nef reflection proves psh descent without assuming envelopes on X. Finite normalization preserves the ample degree and energy, so actual-X finite-energy MA is the raw root-plus-Stieltjes measure. Its inverse integrates the measure tails. Squared-tail finiteness is exactly the dual energy condition, excludes endpoint mass, and gives uniqueness modulo one constant. The proof transports compactness and envelopes only after establishing the cone isomorphism, checks envelope differentiation and comparison, and states bounded-reference dependence. The sector is one-dimensional and trivially valued, not the complete original axis.
notes.text:
Theorem, a partial result. Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero with the trivial valuation, X an integral projective unibranch k-curve, and L an ample line bundle of degree V>0 on actual X. Integrality retains reducedness and connectedness; the field is complete. Use the canonical trivial metric and normalized intersection energy E(0)=0, E(φ+c)=E(φ)+c. No smoothness or normality of X, reducedness of its conductor, atomicity or skeletal support is assumed. The genuine raw finite-energy MA has mass V. It induces a bijection E¹(X,L)/R onto positive Radon μ of raw mass V with E*(μ/V)=sup_{φ∈E¹}(E(φ)−V⁻¹∫φ dμ)<∞. Here E¹ consists of actual-X psh potentials with E>−∞. The proof uses the precisely scoped published background of n1.

Normalization and PL descent. The normalization ν:Y→X is finite; Y is smooth because k is perfect and Y is a normal curve. Properness centers every valuation of the common function field. At a closed point q of Y the local DVR makes every nontrivial valuation t ord_q, t>0; the other analytic points are the common trivial root o and closed-support endpoints q∞. Unibranchness gives one q over each p∈X(k), with the same residue field k. Thus ν^an bijects both generic-support valuations and endpoints. Compactness of the source and Hausdorffness of the target make it a homeomorphism.

Let m_p O_{Y,q}=m_q^{e_p}, 1≤e_p<∞. Away from q the extended point ideal is the unit ideal. For rational a>0 the actual-X flag-ideal function h_{p,a}=e_p⁻¹ max(log|m_p|,−e_p a) pulls back to −min(t,a) on the q-ray and zero on every other ray. It belongs to PL(X) by BJ Example 2.5. Those functions and rational constants span PL(Y) by Example 2.6. Hence ν* identifies PL(X) with PL(Y), also over R. The conductor Ann(ν*O_Y/O_X) has finite support and may be nonreduced. No arbitrary section or power descent is used; e_p is the point-ideal order, not a conductor exponent. The single branch is essential to the isolated-ray identity.

Polarization and positivity. The quotient in 0→O_X→ν*O_Y→T→0 has finite length. Tensoring by L^m and comparing the linear coefficients of χ(Y,(ν*L)^m) and χ(X,L^m) proves deg_Y ν*L=V. On a projective integral curve positive degree is ample, so the upstairs datum is genuinely ample, with no mass multiplier. Canonical reference metrics pull back because local trivializations at centers pull back.

For a descended PL function, resolve only the graph of its model pullback to obtain a projective surjective morphism of test configurations. A pulled-back nef class is nef; conversely each vertical curve downstairs has a curve upstairs dominating it, obtained by projective hyperplane cuts. The pullback degree is a positive degree multiple of the downstairs degree, so nefness reflects. Common dominating models preserve the property. This applies BJ Proposition 3.6(vi) after, not before, proving PL descent. Approximate any psh function on Y decreasingly by H_dom(Y,ν*L). Its PL approximants descend and are nef-psh on actual X; decreasing closure gives psh descent. Ordinary pullback supplies the reverse inclusion. Thus ν* is a psh-cone isomorphism and a weak homeomorphism, since divisorial valuations of the common function field are identified. No envelope property on X has been assumed.

Energy and operator. Write a=φ(o), b_q(t)=−φ'_q(t) almost everywhere. The smooth-curve criterion, now valid on actual X by the cone isomorphism, says that b_q≥0 is nonincreasing, Σ_q b_q(0+)≤V, and φ_q(t)=a−∫₀ᵗb_q. Endpoints have the limiting values, possibly −∞. Only countably many rays are nonconstant. For model PL potentials the genuine raw intersection measure is Vδ_o+Δφ and integration by parts gives E(φ)=a−D(φ)/(2V), D(φ)=Σ_q∫₀∞b_q². Model energy projection follows from the normalization fundamental-cycle projection formula, so no conductor boundary term is omitted.

Approximate b_q increasingly from below by nonincreasing rational step functions on finitely many rays and bounded intervals, using refining dyadic right-endpoint samples and rounding down. Their initial budgets stay ≤V. Their integrals are decreasing PL psh approximants, including at endpoints. Monotone energy extension and monotone convergence give the same energy formula for every psh φ. Thus E¹ is exactly D(φ)<∞. These approximants can also be replaced by actual H_dom(X,L): if f_n↓φ and ||h_n−f_n||∞≤ε_n=2⁻ⁿ, the potentials h_n+3ε_n decrease and have the same limit. Proposition 3.10 supplies h_n in the fixed ample class.

Finite D forces b_q(∞)=0. The raw operator is consequently (V−Σ b_q(0+))δ_o+Σ_q(−db_q)|_(0,∞), transported through ν to actual X. Each positive Stieltjes ray measure has mass b_q(0+); the total is exactly V and endpoints have no mass. The countable sum is Radon, with total-variation tails tending to zero. It agrees with model intersection MA and hence with the unique published decreasing finite-energy extension, by density of actual-X PL test functions. Energy projection extends decreasingly, identifying E¹ spaces and giving MA_raw,X(φ)=ν* MA_raw,Y(ν*φ). This identifies genuine MA, not another inverse measure construction.

Measure energy and inverse. Rays minus o, including endpoints, are disjoint open subsets. A compact subset of their union meets finitely many rays; Radon inner regularity therefore concentrates any finite μ away from o on countably many rays. For raw mass V let μ_q be its ray restriction and τ_q(t)=μ_q((t,∞]), including possible endpoint mass. Put D(μ)=Σ∫τ_q². Endpoint mass forces D(μ)=∞. Tonelli gives −∫(φ−a)dμ=Σ∫b_qτ_q. When D(μ)<∞, Cauchy–Schwarz proves integrability of every finite-energy potential, and completing the square gives E(φ)−V⁻¹∫φdμ≤D(μ)/(2V). Conversely the continuous psh tests with slopes τ_q 1_[0,T) on a finite set F of rays have initial budget ≤V and objective (2V)⁻¹Σ_{q∈F}∫₀ᵀτ_q². Let F,T increase. This proves E*(μ/V)=D(μ)/(2V), including the infinite case. Uniform H_dom approximation of those tests, and decreasing approximation plus monotone integration for all E¹ tests, proves equivalence of the two suprema.

When D(μ)<∞ define φ(o)=0 and φ_q(t)=−∫₀ᵗτ_q(s)ds=−∫min(t,u)dμ_q(u), with endpoint limits. The finite F,T tests decrease to it, so it is psh on actual X. Its energy is −D(μ)/(2V). Its Stieltjes measures are precisely μ_q and its root coefficient is μ({o}), giving MA_raw(φ)=μ. Conversely any finite-energy solution has −db_q=μ_q and b_q(∞)=0, hence b_q=τ_q. These slopes determine every value, including endpoint limits, up to the root constant. This proves necessity and uniqueness, without first solving upstairs and assuming descent.

Required analytic replacements. The weak normalized psh cone on actual X is homeomorphic to the smooth Y cone, which is compact by BJ Theorems 5.20/5.11. Homeomorphism commutes with usc regularization, and the proved cone bijection identifies all envelope competitors: ν*P_X(f)=P_Y(ν*f). Thus envelopes and their continuity descend, without a circular target-envelope assumption. The quadratic energy differentiates along E¹ segments to V⁻¹∫(ψ−φ)MA_raw(φ). BJ Theorem 8.5 gives downward-energy differentiation for actual-X PL variations without smoothness; the now-proved envelope property identifies downward energy with E(P(φ+tf)). Uniform PL approximation and |f−f_m|≤ε_m bound perturbed energy errors by |t|ε_m, proving d/dt|₀ E(P(φ+tf))=V⁻¹∫f MA_raw(φ) for every continuous f. For u=P(f), P(u+t(f−u))=u, 0≤t≤1, so differentiation also proves envelope orthogonality ∫(f−u)MA_raw(u)=0.

BJ locality for finite-energy maxima applies to the identified genuine operator. Equal raw mass and locality for max(φ,ψ−ε), followed by ε↓0, give ∫_{φ<ψ}MA_raw(ψ)≤∫_{φ<ψ}MA_raw(φ). The potential negative-infinite loci here are endpoints with zero MA mass. Published decreasing continuity holds for every finite-energy approximating net, not only the chosen steps; Proposition 12.7 gives strong continuity. The cone/energy identifications preserve weak-plus-energy strong potential topology and weak-plus-dual-energy strong measure topology. The completed-square bound is attained by the constructed inverse, proving actual variational attainment.

For a continuous semipositive reference ρ, the same metric has relative energy E_ρ(φ−ρ)=E(φ)−E(ρ), by the energy cocycle and decreasing extension. Its dual energy becomes E*(μ/V)−E(ρ)+V⁻¹∫ρdμ, a finite change. Thus finite energy is independent of these bounded reference changes. One additive real constant is the correct uniqueness ambiguity because X is integral.

Complete details and original residual obligations are in P16.1-argument.md and standalone P16.1-paper.tex; the compiled paper is build/P16.1-paper.pdf (11 pages). Run bash rerun.sh. Both actual TeX passes returned 0; the final pass has no warnings. Exact rational examples with V=5 give D(μ)=8, E(φ)=−4/5, dual objective 4/5, and both segment-derivative computations 4/5; point-ideal orders e=1,2,3,7 give the stated isolated-ray identity. These are finite consistency observations, not a proof verification. Actual logs and outputs are in build/, curve-checks.json and checks.json. This theorem restricts dimension to one and uses the trivial field endpoint; it does not complete the original P16.1.

notes.summary: Nodal obstruction and explicit remaining gaps: raw mass plus standard finite dual energy does not suffice on all singular curves. A mass-V divisorial atom forces unequal normalization endpoint values over a node. Higher-dimensional unibranch envelopes and the discretely valued singular equation package remain unproved; status is partial and candidate=false.
notes.detailedSummary: On an integral projective nodal curve over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, μ=Vδ_ord(q1) has finite actual-X dual energy at most V/2, but has no actual-X finite-energy solution. The unique normalization solution drops by V at one preimage of the node and by zero at the other, contradicting fiber constancy. This prevents an unrestricted singular theorem with the usual measure condition. The draft leaves higher-dimensional PL/psh/conductor descent, unibranch envelope regularity, the nontrivial discrete-valuation finite-energy operator and analytic-input replacements, and a corrected branched-measure range unresolved. All required deliverables and twice-run TeX diagnostics are retained.
notes.text:
Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero. Let X be an integral projective curve with an ordinary node p, let L be ample of raw degree V, and let q1,q2 be its two normalization preimages. Put μ=Vδ_v, v=ord_q1 viewed on X^an. This has the exact required raw mass. Any psh potential on actual X pulls back to Y; model projection and decreasing energy extension preserve its energy, even though pullback need not be onto. Thus E*_X(δ_v)≤E*_Y(δ_ord_q1)=V/2, by n2's smooth-curve tail calculation at t=1. Hence μ is a genuine finite-energy measure on actual X.

Suppose it were MA_raw,X(φ) for φ∈E¹(X,L). Published normalization pushforward identifies its upstairs MA. Normalization is injective at finite generic-support ray points, and finite-energy MA has no endpoint mass; therefore that upstairs measure is exactly Vδ_ord_q1. By the explicit slope uniqueness in n2, its potential is a−V min(t,1) on the q1-ray and constant a on the q2-ray. The endpoint values are a−V and a. Both endpoints map to p, while a pulled-back function must have equal values on a fiber. This is a contradiction. No arbitrary measure restriction was normalized, and no unproved potential descent was used. This is the raw-mass version of BJ Example 12.11, with its obstruction proved here.

The positive theorem therefore retains unibranchness and integrality. On disconnected spaces the component polarization masses must be fixed separately and uniqueness has a constant per component. On branched singular spaces even the mass and standard finite-energy condition are insufficient, as above; a changed range condition needs an explicit conductor-compatible theory.

The whole original atom remains open in this draft. The curve generator argument does not prove higher-dimensional PL or psh descent. Topological normalization homeomorphism alone supplies none of semipositivity, approximation, energy identity for arbitrary upstairs potentials, or envelopes. In the exact trivial-field source, unibranch envelopes remain Conjecture 5.14 and Theorem 12.8 makes their proof the missing general existence input. This is a statement about the inspected version, not an assertion of absence of later theorems outside the authorized caches. Pullback of an ample datum to a resolution can be nonample, so no smooth ample-class theorem was silently applied there. No singular-space finite-energy equation package is established here over the nontrivially discretely valued residue-characteristic-zero endpoint; the BFJ v1 algebraizability and SNC-support assumptions cannot be erased. A corrected measure range on non-unibranch varieties and the general conductor descents also remain unsupplied.
